source_purpose.quote:
Upper Karha watershed from semi-arid part of Deccan Volcanic Province, India
was investigated to identify the potential sites to construct rainwater harvesting structures
with the help of remote sensing and geographical information system.

supporting_native_excerpts.locator: cached PDF page 1; native text slice
supporting_native_excerpts.quote:
geomorphology, geology were considered as per Integrated Mission for Sustainable Devel-
opment specifications for identification of the structures. The thematic layers overlaid using
intersection based on these specifications. Derived sites were investigated for its suitability
and implementation by ground truth field verification.

supporting_native_excerpts.locator: cached PDF page 4; native text slice
supporting_native_excerpts.quote:
Survey of India toposheets of
1:50,000 scales were used to derive base, contour and drainage map. Digital elevation
model was derived from contour layer and validated with differential global position-
ing system surveyed points and survey of India toposheet. The drainage map was
generated from the toposheets and updated using satellite data and digital elevation
model using Arc soil water assessment tool (Arc SWAT). Horton (1945) method of
stream ordering was adopted for giving order to drainage.

supporting_native_excerpts.locator: cached PDF page 11; native text slice
supporting_native_excerpts.quote:
Maps of different thematic layer were integrated using intersection tool based on priority.
Different structures were identified (Fig. 8) on the basis of specification adopted from
Table 6. Settlement buffer map was overlaid to check that no rainwater harvesting structure
lies within 500 m of settlement area.

visual_checks: Table 6 and Figure 8, PDF14 / printed p2550: all four structure rows, catchment-area header in hectares and other columns checked against rendered page.

retained_profile.quantity: Contributing catchment area associated with the candidate structure, in hectares
retained_profile.lineage: Adopted specifications attributed to IMSD (1995) in Table 6. The study applies them in Upper Karha, semi-arid basaltic western India, by intersecting layers and checking derived sites against field observations. One linked study carries this guidance. No independent validation of the area breakpoints is reported here.
retained_profile.source_weight: No numeric catchment-area weight or suitability scores reported for the adopted specifications. The recipe default weight does not come from Table 6.
retained_profile.numeric_plausibility: One hectare appears in the lower end of the printed farm-pond band. A single family-wide minimum cannot encode the upper end or the other structures. Preserve the literal check-dam >25 comparator, the two printed bands, and the gully-plug dash. The paper does not give an uncertainty tolerance, scores, interpolation, or a general direction across structures.
retained_profile.spatial_support: Mapped sites in Fig.8. Methods PDF4 describe 1:50,000 Survey of India topographic sheets and contour-derived DEM, satellite and ArcSWAT-updated drainage. Local contributing-area delineation/outlet handling for individual structures is not fully specified. Catchment is not the installed structure footprint, total watershed extent or distance to a watercourse.

claims.source_review_note: Kadam et al. (2012), Table 6 (PDF14, printed p2550), maps potential sites using IMSD (1995) specifications. Catchment means land draining to a candidate structure. Farm ponds use 1–2 ha of contributing land, check dams >25 ha, and percolation tanks 25–40 ha. Gully-plug area is unspecified. Slope, runoff, land use, stream order and soil also differ by structure. The current T4 row applies a 1 ha minimum to the whole family.
claims.dashboard_reason: Next mapping review. Kadam et al. (2012) use upstream contributing area to select sites by structure. Table 6 (PDF p. 14), adopted from IMSD (1995), gives 1–2 ha for farm ponds, strictly >25 ha for check dams, and 25–40 ha for percolation tanks. The gully-plug cell shows a dash. Each area condition is paired with stream order, slope, runoff, land use and soil.

dataset_fitness.status: No configured input for this mapping. No approved binding hold is claimed here. Numerical and dataset decisions are distinct.
dataset_fitness.required_quantity: Upstream drainage area at each candidate outlet, converted to ha. Select a suitable local flow network or derive accumulation at native resolution, account for actual cell area when converting counts, then aggregate if needed. Small features, local drainage and outlet alignment matter for 1–2 ha ponds.

existing_catalog_entry_for_different_use.fitness_diagnosis: The upa band could represent the physical quantity after km² × 100 = ha. At nominal equatorial spacing, one cell is about 0.86 ha; a 1–2 ha contributing area spans only about 1–2 nominal pixel areas there, with actual cell area varying by latitude. This is a scale comparison, not a measured error or evidence that any specific local site is unusable. Small-catchment fitness remains unverified. No binding or provider selection proposed.

dashboard_question: Should we hold the shared 1 ha minimum and retain the complete structure-specific table for synthesis? The 1 ha boundary belongs to the farm-pond range. Gully-plug area is unspecified. Applying the table would also require a compatible upstream contributing-area layer at the intended site scale. This decision concerns numerical calibration.
